confirmed.title: escapeHtml() does not escape quotes, so an announcement's Image URL / link / title breaks out of the surrounding HTML attribute and executes script in every viewer's session (stored XSS)
confirmed.workflow: Create announcement -> student views feed/detail
confirmed.role: clubCore, schoolRep (attacker); student, clubCore, schoolRep, superAdmin (victim)
confirmed.evidence: js/utils.js:202-207 — `export function escapeHtml(str) { ... const div = document.createElement("div"); div.textContent = str; return div.innerHTML; }`. The HTML text-node serializer only escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and U+00A0 — it does NOT escape `"` or `'`. Every announcement renderer interpolates this into *quoted attribute* positions: js/ui.js:1225 ``; js/ui.js:1234 ``; js/ui.js:1240 `data-title="${escapeHtml(item.title)}"`; js/ui.js:1675 (home page card) `data-title="${escapeHtml(item.title)}"`. The only input validation is a prefix test that cannot stop a quote: js/main.js:771 `if (imageUrl && !/^https?:\/\//.test(imageUrl))` and js/validation.js:19 the same regex — `https://a.png" onerror="...` passes both. The value is stored verbatim by createAnnouncement (js/services.js:1039-1045) and injected via `app.innerHTML = ...` (js/ui.js:9).
confirmed.repro: 1) Sign in as an approved club core member (state.host.approved true). 2) Top bar -> Create -> Create Announcement. 3) Title `Fest`, Description `x`, Image URL: `https://a.png" onerror="alert(document.domain)`. 4) Click Post Announcement — the /^https?:\/\// check passes, the doc is written and appears in the feed. 5) Sign in as any student, go to Announcements, click that card. renderAnnouncementDetail emits ``; the image 404s, onerror fires, arbitrary JS runs on the app origin. The same works with a title of `x" onmouseover="alert(1)" data-z="` which lands in the data-title attribute of the Save/Report buttons on the Home page (js/ui.js:1675), firing for every student on the landing screen without any click.
confirmed.impact: Any approved club core member or school rep (i.e. any student who got core approval for one club) can run arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every student, other host, and super admin who views the announcement — on the same origin as the authenticated Firebase session, so it can read/write Firestore as the victim (including admin.html actions if a super admin views it). Stored and persistent for 30 days.
confirmed.fix: Add a real attribute escaper and use it in attribute positions: `export function escapeAttr(s){return escapeHtml(s).replace(/"/g,'"').replace(/'/g,''');}` (or make escapeHtml itself replace `&<>"'` by string substitution instead of textContent/innerHTML round-trip) and apply it at js/ui.js:1225, 1234, 1240, 1675 and the other `data-title=`/`src=`/`href=` interpolations. Additionally validate URLs with `new URL()` + protocol allow-list in js/validation.js instead of a prefix regex.

confirmed.title: users/{uid} create rule constrains only `role` and `email`, so any student can self-grant `schoolRepApproved: true` on first write and become a school representative
confirmed.workflow: Role elevation / school-representative hosting (hostRequests + admin approval)
confirmed.evidence:
firestore.rules:89-93 — the create rule has no `hasOnly()` field whitelist:
```
allow create: if isRvuEmail()
  && createsOwnDoc(uid)
  && request.resource.data.role == 'student'
  && request.resource.data.email is string
  && request.resource.data.email.lower() == authEmailKey();
```
Every other field in the payload is unconstrained. `schoolRepApproved` is exactly the field the rules trust as a role grant — firestore.rules:58-61 inside `isApprovedSchoolRep()`:
```
|| ( exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(request.auth.uid))
     && get(/databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(request.auth.uid)).data.schoolRepApproved == true )
```
and `isApprovedSchoolRep()` is the sole gate on school-wide content at firestore.rules:240 (events create), :246 (events update), :250 (events delete), :264 (announcements create), :270 (announcements update), :274 (announcements delete).

The update rule correctly protects the field (firestore.rules:103 `unchanged('schoolRepApproved')`) and the self-heal branch correctly requires an approved canonical host request (firestore.rules:114-118), but the CREATE path has no such protection, so the whole approval chain is bypassable at document birth.

The client then trusts the flag with no server-side re-verification: js/services.js:642 `if (!schoolAccesses.length && (profile.schoolRepApproved === true || ...))` pushes a synthetic school access, and js/services.js:1528 `const flagOk = profile.schoolRepApproved === true;` makes `assertCanCreateSchoolContent()` return true at js/services.js:1534.
confirmed.repro:
Role: student, using any @rvu.edu.in Google account that has NOT yet signed in to RVU Connect (so `users/{uid}` does not exist — this is every incoming student at Friday launch).
1. Load the Firebase JS SDK in a scratch local HTML file using the app's shipped public config from js/config.js (client Firebase keys are public by design, so this needs no secrets).
2. `signInWithPopup(auth, new GoogleAuthProvider())` with the RVU account. Do NOT open RVU Connect — that would run `ensureUserProfile()` (js/services.js:319) and create the doc first.
3. `await setDoc(doc(db,'users',uid), { role:'student', email:'me@rvu.edu.in', name:'me', schoolRepApproved:true, schoolScope:'SOCSE' })`. This is a CREATE, so firestore.rules:89-93 applies: role is 'student' ✓, email matches ✓, `schoolRepApproved` is never inspected → WRITE SUCCEEDS.
4. Open RVU Connect and sign in normally. `ensureUserProfile` takes the `snap.exists()` branch (js/services.js:301) and returns the tampered profile untouched. `loadCampusData` js/services.js:642 pushes a schoolAccess; js/auth.js:279-290 sets `state._hasSchoolRep = true` and `state.host.approved = true`.
5. Create → switch host mode to School → publish a school announcement or school event. `assertCanCreateSchoolContent()` passes (js/services.js:1528/1534) and the Firestore write is allowed by firestore.rules:240 / :264 via the `schoolRepApproved` branch.
6. Open any existing official school announcement or event and click Report/Delete: main.js:868 `delete-school-event` and main.js:876 `delete-school-announcement` are gated only on `isSchoolRep()`, and firestore.rules:250 / :274 allow the delete for any `isApprovedSchoolRep()`.
confirmed.impact: Full self-service escalation from student to school representative with zero admin involvement — the entire hostRequests → super-admin-approval workflow is bypassed. The attacker can publish campus-wide 'school' events and announcements that appear as official RVU communications to every student, and can UPDATE or DELETE every school-hosted event and announcement on the platform, including legitimate notices posted by real school reps and by super admins (permanent data loss — `deleteDocument` is a hard delete, js/services.js:1206). Because `isApprovedSchoolRep()` is campus-wide with no per-school scoping in the rules, the blast radius is the whole institution. Not escalatable to superAdmin (create still forces role=='student' and `superAdmins/{uid}` requires `isSuperAdmin()`), so it caps at school rep.
confirmed.fix:
Add a field whitelist to the create rule so a new profile can only carry non-privileged fields. In firestore.rules replace lines 89-93 with:
```
allow create: if isRvuEmail()
  && createsOwnDoc(uid)
  && request.resource.data.role == 'student'
  && request.resource.data.email is string
  && request.resource.data.email.lower() == authEmailKey()
  && !request.resource.data.keys().hasAny(['schoolRepApproved','clubCoreApproved','schoolScope','hostApproved'])
  && request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly(['email','name','role','clubIds','roleTitle','interests','onboardingComplete','school','year','createdAt','updatedAt']);
```
The `hasOnly` list matches exactly the profile object built in js/services.js:310-318, so `ensureUserProfile` keeps working unchanged. Keep the existing update-rule protections as they are.

confirmed.title: clubs/{clubId}/coreMembers read rule has no branch for non-members, so the 'Club core team' roster on every club page is permanently empty for every student
confirmed.workflow: Club directory → club detail page → Club core team roster
confirmed.evidence:
firestore.rules:166-173 — the read rule has exactly three branches and none of them can be true for a signed-in student who is not on that club's roster: ``` allow read: if isSuperAdmin() || (isRvuEmail() && ( memberEmail == request.auth.token.email || memberEmail == authEmailKey() || resource.data.uid == request.auth.uid || (resource.data.email is string && resource.data.email.lower() == authEmailKey()) )) || isApprovedClubCore(clubId); ``` The middle branch is per-document and only ever matches the caller's OWN membership doc. The client performs a **collection list**, not a get — js/services.js:1169: ``` const snap = await getDocs(collection(db, "clubs", clubId, "coreMembers")); ``` Firestore evaluates the read rule against each candidate document and rejects the entire list if any document fails, so as soon as the club has one core member who is not the caller, the whole `getDocs` is denied. There is no unconditional branch (e.g. 'any signed-in RVU user may read the roster of an approved club') and no `isClubFounder(clubId)` branch either. The UI renders this section unconditionally for all roles — js/ui.js:854-876 is outside every `canEdit` guard: ```

Club core team

${state._clubCoreMembersLoading ? "Loading…" : `${coreMembers.length} member...`} ... : renderEmptyState("No core members listed", "Approved club core members will appear here.") ``` The denial is swallowed: js/main.js:388-391 `.catch(() => { state.clubCoreMembers = []; ... })` and js/router.js:67-68 `catch (_) { state.clubCoreMembers = []; }`.
confirmed.repro:
Role: student (any signed-in student who is not core of the club being viewed — i.e. essentially the entire user base for essentially every club).
1. Sign in as a normal student.
2. Go to Clubs and click any club card (`data-action="open-club"`, handler js/main.js:379-394). Equivalently, open the deep link `?route=clubs&clubSlug=<clubId>` which hits js/router.js:66.
3. js/main.js:384 calls `listClubCoreMembers(clubId)`. Inside, js/services.js:1165 `ensureCoreMembersFromApprovedApps` is denied first (clubApplications read, firestore.rules:212-215, none of the branches hold for a student) and swallowed at js/services.js:1166-1168.
4. js/services.js:1169 `getDocs(collection(db,'clubs',clubId,'coreMembers'))` throws `permission-denied` (console shows 'Missing or insufficient permissions').
5. js/main.js:389 sets `state.clubCoreMembers = []`, and js/ui.js:875 renders the section header '0 members' plus the empty state 'No core members listed'.
confirmed.impact: The 'Club core team' section — a headline feature of the club detail page, and the only place a student can see who to contact about a club — shows '0 members' and 'No core members listed' for every club, for every student, always. It fails silently: no error state, no retry, no explanation, and the section still claims members 'will appear here'. Club core members and super admins see the correct roster, so this will not reproduce for whoever demos the app, only for the actual student audience. It also fires a permission-denied on every single club page view for every student.
confirmed.fix:
Add a branch to the coreMembers read rule that does not depend on `resource.data`, so the list operation is satisfiable for ordinary students. In firestore.rules, at line 166, insert before the per-document branch:
```
allow read: if isSuperAdmin()
  || (isRvuEmail()
      && exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/clubs/$(clubId))
      && get(/databases/$(database)/documents/clubs/$(clubId)).data.status == 'approved')
  || isClubFounder(clubId)
  || (isRvuEmail() && ( ...existing per-document branch... ))
  || isApprovedClubCore(clubId);
```
The roster is already rendered publicly including member emails (js/ui.js:869-870), so exposing it to signed-in RVU users for approved clubs matches the intended product behaviour. The added `isClubFounder(clubId)` branch also fixes the founder case.

confirmed.title: Founder who clicks 'Leave club core' keeps the full club-management UI via the founderEmail fallback, but every clubs/{clubId} write is then denied — a permanent dead-end for the club's owner
confirmed.workflow: Club management: leave club core / edit club profile / toggle registration / post club events
confirmed.repro:
Role: clubCore (specifically the club's founder — created by 'Request a new club' → super admin Approve, which sets `founderEmail` to the requester's email at js/services.js:907).
1. Sign in as the founder. Go to Clubs → your club. The management buttons render (js/ui.js:820-824).
2. Click 'Leave club core' (js/ui.js:823) and confirm the dialog (js/main.js:1195).
3. Toast says 'You left club core for this club.' Then js/main.js:1215 soft-refreshes, the founderEmail fallback re-adds the club, and 'Edit club profile' / 'Close registration' / 'Leave club core' are STILL displayed on the club page.
4. Click 'Close registration'. js/main.js:404-410 optimistically flips the label to 'Registration closed', then `updateClubRegistration` → `updateDoc(clubs/{id})` is denied by firestore.rules:162 → js/main.js:411-414 reverts the label and rethrows. The button visibly toggles and snaps back.
5. Click 'Edit club profile' → change the tagline → 'Save changes'. `canManageClub` passes (js/main.js:1516), then `updateClubProfile` (js/services.js:1198) is denied → js/main.js:1546 shows the toast 'Missing or insufficient permissions.'
6. Create → Club event: the club host mode is still offered, but `createEvent` with `hostType:'club'` is denied by firestore.rules:239 (`isApprovedClubCore`).
7. Clicking 'Leave club core' again 'succeeds' (deleting an absent doc is a no-op) and changes nothing — there is no way back to a working state from inside the app.
confirmed.impact: The club's own founder is left with a fully visible but completely non-functional management console: every edit, the registration toggle, and all club event/announcement posting fail with raw 'Missing or insufficient permissions' toasts, and 'Leave club core' can never be undone from the UI. Only a super admin re-running Assign core role can repair it, and the founder has no signal that that is what is needed. The same rules gap makes two more founder actions inconsistent even before leaving: `assignClubCoreRole` succeeds for a founder (firestore.rules:179 includes `isClubFounder`) while `removeClubCoreRole` is denied (firestore.rules:189-191 has no `isClubFounder` branch), so a founder can add core members but not remove them.
confirmed.fix:
Two changes, both small. (1) Make the rules agree with the client's founder fallback — in firestore.rules add `isClubFounder(clubId)` to the clubs write rule (line 162) and to the coreMembers delete rule (line 189):
```
allow update: if isSuperAdmin() || ((isApprovedClubCore(clubId) || isClubFounder(clubId)) && unchanged('createdAt') && unchanged('createdBy'));
...
allow delete: if isSuperAdmin() || isApprovedClubCore(clubId) || isClubFounder(clubId) || (isRvuEmail() && (memberEmail == request.auth.token.email || memberEmail == authEmailKey()));
```
(2) Stop offering 'Leave club core' to the founder, since the founder grant is not revocable — in js/ui.js:823 render that button only when the access is not founder-derived, e.g. guard on `state.host.clubAccesses.find(a => (a.club?.id||a.club?.slug) === (club.id||club.slug))?.member?.role !== 'founder'`.

confirmed.title: projects/{projectId}/applications has no rule at all, so the admin 'Export Applicants' button always fails with a permission error
confirmed.workflow: Super-admin console → Projects tab → Export project applicants
confirmed.evidence:
firestore.rules:277-289 is `match /projects/{projectId} { ... }` with no nested `match` for subcollections. Firestore rules do not cascade to subcollections, so `projects/{projectId}/applications/{docId}` falls through to the catch-all at firestore.rules:316-318:
```
match /{document=**} {
  allow read, write: if false;
}
```
The client reads exactly that path — js/services.js:1323:
```
const snap = await getDocs(collection(db, "projects", projectId, "applications"));
```
The button is rendered on every project row in the admin console — admin.js:709:
```
<button class="mini-btn" data-action="export-project-applicants" data-id="${project.id}">Export Applicants</button>
```
and the handler has no try/catch — admin.js:1114-1118 — so it surfaces through admin.js:1183-1185 `.catch((error) => { window.alert(error.message || "Action failed."); })`.

Note also that js/services.js:129-135 (`ruleTraceFor`) confidently documents a rule for `projects/{projectId}/applications/{uid}` ('create uid path segment must equal auth.uid', 'update requires super admin or project owner') that does not exist anywhere in firestore.rules — the debug trace will actively mislead whoever investigates this.
confirmed.repro:
Role: superAdmin.
1. Sign in as a super admin (js/auth.js:348 redirects to admin.html).
2. Click the 'Projects' tab (admin.js:363, dispatched at admin.js:430).
3. On any project row click 'Export Applicants' (admin.js:709).

confirmed.title: The 12-second background poll re-runs loadCampusData and resets both the feed and the pagination cursor, undoing every Load More click

confirmed.role: student with a pending club application or pending host request, pending clubCore, pending schoolRep
confirmed.evidence: js/auth.js:100-122 startPendingAccessPolling sets `_pendingAccessPoll = window.setInterval(async () => { ... await softRefreshCampusData({ showSkeleton: false }); ... }, 12000)`. softRefreshCampusData (js/auth.js:87-95) calls syncFirebaseData, which at js/auth.js:246-250 does `const data = await window.RVUFirebase.loadCampusData(...)` then `replaceCollection(events, data.events.map(normalizeEvent)); replaceCollection(announcements, data.announcements); replaceCollection(projects, data.projects);` — wholesale replacement with page 1. loadCampusData also resets the module-level cursor at js/services.js:479-481 (`lastDocs.events = eventsSnap.docs[...]`), which is the exact cursor loadMore reads at js/services.js:1557-1562. The poll is started on the pending paths at js/main.js:277, :314, :338, :1418 and js/auth.js:357-359, and stopPendingAccessPolling is only reached on approval (js/auth.js:113) or sign-out (js/auth.js:391), so it runs for the whole session.

Sign in as a student and apply to a club (data-action='submit-club-application'), or submit a school-rep request — js/main.js:1418 / js/auth.js:358 start the poll because state.clubApplications contains a pending row. 2. Go to Events and click Load More (js/ui.js:679). 40 events render. 3. Wait up to 12 seconds without touching anything. The poll fires, syncFirebaseData replaces `events` with the first 20 again, and render() redraws the truncated list. 4. confirmed.title: loadMore reports 'No more items to load' when the page was actually fetched and discarded, or when the query failed

confirmed.evidence: js/services.js:1567 `const snap = await getDocs(q).catch(() => ({ docs: [] }));` swallows every error into an empty page. js/services.js:1568-1577 then advances the cursor and post-filters the page: `if (collectionName === "announcements") result = result.filter((item) => !isAnnouncementExpired(item)); if (collectionName === "events") result = result.filter((item) => !isEventExpired(item))...`. The caller at js/main.js:905-908 treats an empty array as end-of-list: `if (newItems.length === 0) { ...toast 'No more items to load.' ; return; }`. Note the projects branch (js/services.js:1561-1562) applies no expiry filter at all, unlike loadCampusData:511-523.
confirmed.repro: Case A (false end-of-list): with 60 published events where events 21-40 by createdAt all have past dates, click Load More on Events. Page 2 is fetched, every row is dropped by isEventExpired, result is [], and the toast says 'No more items to load.' — while 20 live events sit on page 3, now unreachable because the button reports the list is exhausted. Case B (failure as emptiness): go offline and click Load More. getDocs rejects, the catch returns {docs: []}, and the user gets the same 'No more items to load.' with no error indication. Case C (inconsistency): create a project with expiry set to yesterday so loadCampusData:511-523 hides it, then click Load More on Projects — the expired project is appended and rendered, until the 60s expiry poll (js/auth.js:148-157) silently removes it again.

confirmed.fix: Loop or re-query until the filtered page is non-empty (or the raw page is short of `limit`), and distinguish the three outcomes: raw `snap.docs.length === 0` -> 'no more items'; raw page non-empty but fully filtered -> fetch the next page; rejected promise -> let it throw and show an error toast. confirmed.title: Every read failure in loadCampusData is swallowed into an empty array with no user-visible error, and the error plumbing (handleFirebaseError) is never called anywhere
confirmed.workflow: Campus data sync / all feed pages
confirmed.evidence: js/services.js:474-476 attaches `.catch(() => ({ docs: [] }))` to the events, announcements and projects queries. js/services.js:266-275 rowsOrEmpty returns [] on any error and, for the most likely error, logs nothing at all: `if (error?.code !== "permission-denied") { console.warn(...) } return [];`. That wraps clubs, siteSettings, savedItems, followedClubs, rsvps, clubApplications and hostRequests (js/services.js:484-485, 551-557). js/services.js:4 imports handleFirebaseError and never calls it — grep across js/ and admin.js shows the only call site is js/repository.js:10, and js/repository.js is imported by no file in the project, so js/errors.js is dead code and no Firestore read error ever reaches a toast. loadCampusData exposes no error field and syncFirebaseData (js/auth.js:246-263) unconditionally overwrites state with whatever came back.
confirmed.repro: Sign in as a student and load the app normally, then put the device in airplane mode and press Refresh data (js/main.js:1252-1255, data-action='soft-refresh'). All three feed queries reject with code 'unavailable', the catches return {docs: []}, rowsOrEmpty returns [] for clubs and siteSettings, and js/auth.js:247-250 replaces every collection with []. The user sees the whole campus emptied out with the empty states 'No upcoming events' (js/ui.js:678) / 'No flags' etc., plus a success toast reading 'Campus data refreshed.' confirmed.fix: Let the queries reject and handle it once in syncFirebaseData: catch, call handleFirebaseError (js/errors.js:3) for the toast, set a `state.dataError` flag, and leave the previously loaded collections in place instead of replacing them with []. confirmed.title: Admin 'Export Applicants' reads a subcollection that firestore.rules denies outright, and neither project applications nor event RSVPs are ever written by any code path

confirmed.title: window.alert is globally replaced with a non-blocking modal, and the sign-in error path at auth.js:352 was written assuming it blocks — the app renders and starts polling behind the error dialog

refuted.fix: Wrap every interpolation of Firestore-sourced strings in render-admin.js in the already-imported escapeHtml — lines 285, 301-302, 305, 325, 372, 391, 409, 425 — and note that admin.js's local escapeHtml (admin.js:172-176) does not escape double quotes, so it must not be used for attribute values either (admin.js:834 `value="${escapeHtml(...)}"`).

refuted.title: Admin-tab loader keyed on "array is empty" flashes the full-page skeleton and burns two Firestore reads on every single Admin navigation for clubCore/schoolRep, and never refreshes a non-empty queue
refuted.workflow: Navigating to the Admin tab (club core / school rep dashboard)
refuted.repro:
1. Sign in as an approved clubCore user who has no `hostRequests` doc (approved via the club-application flow — the normal path).
2. Click Admin. Observe the page paint the grey pulsing skeleton (js/ui.js:558-577) before the dashboard appears.
3. Click Home, then Admin again. The skeleton flashes again. Repeat — it flashes on every single Admin navigation, and each time the page is force-scrolled to top twice (renderAtTop at js/router.js:88 and js/router.js:131).
4. In DevTools Network, confirm the `superAdmins/{uid}` + `users/{uid}` reads fire and `loadAdminTab` returns nothing usable.
refuted.impact: Every Admin visit for the two host roles shows a full-page loading skeleton for a request that can only ever return an empty array — the dashboard feels slow and looks like it is re-fetching, and the double scroll-to-top loses the user's place. Combined with the always-true condition it also means the genuinely useful case (a stale non-empty request list) is the one case that never refreshes.
refuted.fix: Replace the emptiness heuristic with explicit per-tab load flags, e.g. `state._adminTabLoaded = {}` keyed by tab name, set after a successful fetch and cleared by the actions that mutate that tab (approve-host / reject-host at js/main.js:417-432 already patch the array locally). Also short-circuit the whole `state.route === "admin"` requests block when `!isSuperAdmin()`, since js/services.js:1582 makes it a guaranteed no-op for clubCore/schoolRep.

refuted.title: resolveOwnClubAccesses fans out one getDoc per approved club and runs twice per sync, so a routine sync costs hundreds of document reads per user
refuted.workflow: Campus data sync / club-core access resolution
refuted.evidence: js/services.js:344 `const candidateIds = new Set((clubs || []).map((c) => c.id).filter(Boolean));` — every approved club, up to the limit(100) at js/services.js:484. js/services.js:353-355 then issues one read per candidate: `await Promise.all([...candidateIds].map(async (clubId) => { const memberSnap = await getDoc(doc(db, "clubs", clubId, "coreMembers", emailKey)); ...`. loadCampusData calls it at js/services.js:560 and, whenever the user has any approved application, a second full time at js/services.js:572-579. ensureOwnCoreMembersFromApplications (js/services.js:406-437) adds a further 2 reads per approved application. Each of those coreMembers reads is evaluated against firestore.rules:166-173, whose fallback branch calls isApprovedClubCore(clubId) (firestore.rules:30-42), itself 2 exists()+get() pairs. All of this repeats on the 12000ms interval at js/auth.js:103-122.
refuted.repro: Seed 100 approved clubs (the ceiling the code already anticipates). Sign in as a club core with one approved application and open the app: loadCampusData issues 100 coreMembers getDoc calls, then 100 more at js/services.js:573, plus the 3 feed queries, clubs, siteSettings, savedItems, followedClubs, rsvps, clubApplications and hostRequests. Now trigger the pending poll (apply to another club) and leave the tab open: that ~210-read sync repeats every 12 seconds, i.e. >1000 document reads per minute for a single idle browser tab.
refuted.impact: Initial load is gated on ~200 sequentially-awaited round trips before the first render completes, which is seconds of blank UI on campus wifi. At real student-body scale the read volume is the dominant cost of the project and will hit Firestore quota/billing long before it hits a functional limit. There is no caching: the same negative lookups are repeated every 12 seconds even though club membership changes approximately never.
refuted.fix: Narrow candidateIds to clubs the user could plausibly be core of — the clubIds already stored on the user profile (js/services.js:326 allows clubIds) plus clubIds from clubApplications — instead of all 100 clubs. Cache the resolved accesses in module state and only re-resolve on an explicit refresh or when clubApplications changes. Delete the duplicate re-resolve at js/services.js:572-579 (the heal at :570 can return its own result). Raise the poll interval well above 12s and have it read only hostRequests/clubApplications for the current uid.
